correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact norm N²=A²+Σ_{j=1}^q s_j², obtained 4W²≥A²+s_1² by averaging squared joint evaluations at (v±y)/√2 with ||S*y||=s_1, and subtracted N²/q to get (q−1)A²/q+Σ_j(s_1²−s_j²)/q≥0. In the orthogonal-source case W=s_1/2 exactly. q>1 equality forces A=0 and rank-q equal nonzero singular values; q=1 requires the separate t-perturbation: averaged squared value t²A²+t(1−t)s_1² has strictly positive derivative A² at t=1/2 unless A=0. Coordinate partial-isometries attain the infimum over both real and complex fields. Under N=1, ε near-minimality yields the stated bounds. Independent deterministic tests use four explicit tight-frame/orthogonal witnesses, one exact q=1 strictness inequality, and 1,400 random real/complex spectral-deficit identities. These do not prove arbitrary dimensions; the analytic argument does.

scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to rank-at-most-one tuples sharing a source. The unrestricted finite-dimensional Hilbert joint index for k≥m is not determined. Priority risk remains around the inaccessible Drnovšek–Müller 2014 article.

value.rationale: The restricted class is the natural common-source rank-one mechanism used in Mal’s Hilbert joint-index sharpness witness. Its exact finite ambient-dimensional saturation at k=m−1 resolves a meaningful parameter regime left by that construction. The complete equality characterization identifies orthogonal systems when k<=m−1 and redundant tight frames when k>=m−1, while a nontrivial spectral deficit controls near-minimizers and source leakage. It is independently useful even without a theorem about arbitrary operator tuples; simple standard matrix inequalities are ingredients but do not by themselves communicate the fixed-m classification.
